requestedActions.title: List active task titles for a connected Todoist account, with pagination
Let customers connect their individual Todoist accounts via OAuth

guide.summary: Use Todoist OAuth with only data:read to list task titles through GET /api/v1/tasks with cursor pagination. Start by registering a test app in the App Management Console and implementing the authorization request, then test with one representative account. Customer-workspace approval and token exchange details are not established in the supplied sources and stay unknown. Avoid write and delete scopes.

findings.title: OAuth authorization is documented for customer connections
findings.detail: Todoist documents an OAuth authorization URL with client_id, scope, state and response_type=code. Redirect URIs are configured in the App Management Console.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.

findings.title: Request data:read for task listing
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks. It is the requested grant for listing active task titles.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Avoid write and delete grants for this read-only use case
findings.detail: Do not request task:add, data:read_write or data:delete. data:read_write also includes task:add and data:read, so it is broader than needed.

evidence.quote: task:add Grants permission to add new tasks (the application cannot read or modify any existing data).
data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
data:delete Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Use cursor pagination for task pages
findings.detail: Request the first page without a cursor, then pass next_cursor as cursor. Keep the same parameters on every page request.

evidence.quote: To fetch the first page of results, make a request without a cursor parameter:
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.

steps.title: Register a test app with a redirect URI in the App Management Console
steps.detail: Create the app in the App Management Console and configure the redirect URI your callback will receive. Keep the client secret in a secure store; do not paste it into shared docs.
steps.doneWhen: The test app exists with a configured redirect URI and a client ID is available.

evidence.quote: This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.
When the user denies your authorization request, Todoist will redirect the user to the configured redirect URI with the error parameter: http://example.com?error=access_denied .

steps.title: Implement the data:read authorization request and callback handling
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with client_id, scope=data:read, state and response_type=code, then handle the callback. Do not execute the flow yet; this step only prepares the code.
steps.doneWhen: The authorization request builds with scope data:read and the callback path is ready for testing.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Authorize one representative test account through the callback
steps.detail: Use a single representative Todoist test account to complete the consent flow in a browser. Confirm the consent screen requests data:read only. The denied path returns error=access_denied to the redirect URI.
steps.doneWhen: The callback receives an authorization code and the test account is connected for the app.

evidence.quote: Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
When the user denies your authorization request, Todoist will redirect the user to the configured redirect URI with the error parameter: http://example.com?error=access_denied .

steps.title: Test first-page active task title listing
steps.detail: Call the tasks endpoint with the connected account token. Expected response: 200 JSON with a results array of tasks and has_more and next_cursor fields. Confirm task title field name from the response. Boundary check: confirm the granted access is data:read only and the request log shows only GET calls.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns 200 with a results array and the title field is identified.

evidence.quote: get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

fields: Access token: backend OAuth exchange for the test account; keep it out of this guide

steps.title: Test the second page using next_cursor
steps.detail: Pass next_cursor from the first response as cursor, keeping limit=50 and all other parameters the same. Expected response: 200 JSON with the next page of results. Boundary check: confirm that only GET requests appear in the request log and no task is modified.
steps.doneWhen: The second page returns 200 with results using the cursor from the first page.

evidence.quote: Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6NTB9.aGFzaA&limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.

fields: Access token: backend OAuth exchange for the test account; keep it out of this guide
